walkthroughs.body_html: Shoreditch transformed since 2000: average house price rose from £150000 to £900000+. Original Bengali community displaced. Hackney gentrification linked to creative industries and Crossrail. Critics cite loss of affordable housing and community character.

Dharavi (Mumbai) houses 700000 people in 2.1 km^2 (density >330000/km^2). Generates $1 billion/yr from recycling, leather, pottery. Redevelopment plans (2022) propose rehousing residents in formal high-rise but raise concerns about livelihood loss.

Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD 2019) ranks LSOAs. Most deprived areas concentrate in north-east England, Liverpool, Birmingham inner city. Gap in life expectancy: 9.5 years between richest and poorest London boroughs (Kensington vs Tower Hamlets).

mcqs.q: What is the main social impact of gentrification?
options: Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Gentrification only has positive effects because it makes areas nicer.
Gentrification means evicting all residents by force.
Displacement of long-term lower-income residents as rents and property prices rise, often along with loss of community businesses and cultural identity — even if the area looks 'improved'.

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: Gentrification means evicting all residents by force.
Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.
People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
